claim: The Subclass 500 Student visa lets a student stay in Australia for up to 6 years and in line with enrolment.
The Subclass 500 Student visa base application charge is from AUD2,000.00.
caveats: Change history: DHA’s 2024 administration report recorded AUD1,600 from 2024-07-01; current 2026 page shows AUD2,000; the exact later change instrument was not surfaced in this session. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The Subclass 500 Student visa can be applied for online in or outside Australia.
A valid Confirmation of Enrolment is required before DHA decides a Subclass 500 Student visa application.
The Genuine Student requirement applies to Student visa applications lodged on or after 23 March 2024.
Future intentions to later apply for permanent residence do not count against an applicant under the Genuine Student requirement.
DHA’s current student-visa framework is the Simplified Student Visa Framework.
caveats: Legacy market language such as “AL3” was not the operative term on the current DHA pages surfaced in this session. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: Under DHA’s evidence-level framework, a student’s evidence level is based on student visas linked to the institution.
The Document Checklist Tool asks for the student’s country of passport.
The Document Checklist Tool asks for the education provider or provider CRICOS code.
A Subclass 500 applicant must show funds for travel costs.
A Subclass 500 applicant must show funds for 12 months of living costs.
A Subclass 500 applicant must show funds for tuition fees for the student and accompanying family members.
A Subclass 500 applicant must show funds for school costs for school-aged dependants.
The current DHA minimum financial-capacity amount for a Student visa primary applicant is AUD29,710.
caveats: Change history on the same DHA page: previous amount AUD24,505. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The current DHA minimum financial-capacity amount for a spouse or de facto partner is AUD10,394.
attribute: financial-capacity amount for spouse/de facto partner
caveats: Change history on the same DHA page: previous amount AUD8,574. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The current DHA minimum financial-capacity amount for a dependent child is AUD4,449.
caveats: Change history on the same DHA page: previous amount AUD3,670. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The current DHA annual school-cost amount is AUD13,502.
caveats: Change history on the same DHA page: previous amount AUD9,661. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: Student visa holders can work up to 48 hours a fortnight when the course is in session.
Family members of a Student visa holder cannot work before the student’s course starts.
Family members of a Student visa holder can work up to 48 hours a fortnight while the course is in session.
caveats: This official page contradicts the common market claim that all partners of degree-level students have unlimited work rights. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: A Student visa holder can work over 48 hours a fortnight only if the visa was granted in relation to a masters degree by research or doctorate degree.
There are no restrictions on the duration of courses a student must study to be accompanied by family members.
Family members of existing Student visa holders who do not already hold a Student visa must apply for a Student visa.
Students under 18 must have welfare arrangements in place until they turn 18.
A student must not enter Australia before welfare arrangements start.
If a provider approves welfare arrangements, the CAAW minimum period must cover the same period as the CoE plus 7 days at the end of enrolment or until the student turns 18.
entity: Confirmation of Appropriate Accommodation and Welfare

claim: The maximum period for a Student visa for primary-school-aged students is generally 3 years.
High-school students in years 7 to 12 may be granted a Student visa for a maximum period of 6 years.
DHA’s median processing time for the Student visa category was 28 days in April 2026.
caveats: Category median, not a Nepal-only or provider-specific band. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: Under DHA student-visa processing priorities, Priority 1 applications are aimed to commence within 1 to 4 weeks of lodgement.
Under DHA student-visa processing priorities, Priority 2 applications are aimed to commence within 5 to 8 weeks of lodgement.
Under DHA student-visa processing priorities, Priority 3 applications are aimed to commence within 9 to 12 weeks of lodgement.
The Subclass 590 Student Guardian visa allows a person to visit Australia for up to 5 years to support a child who holds a Student visa.
The Subclass 590 Student Guardian visa base application charge is from AUD2,000.00.
caveats: Change history: DHA’s 2024 administration report recorded AUD1,600 from 2024-07-01; current 2025/2026 page shows AUD2,000; the exact later change instrument was not surfaced in this session. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: If a guardian is applying to accompany and care for a student under 18, the guardian must prove enough money to support both people.
DHA says a current bank statement is an example of a document that can be attached to prove Subclass 590 financial capacity.
The Temporary Graduate visa remains Subclass 485 in current DHA materials.
The current DHA name of one Subclass 485 stream is Post-Higher Education Work.
The current DHA name of one Subclass 485 stream is Post-Vocational Education Work.
The current DHA name of one Subclass 485 stream is Second Post-Higher Education Work.
The Temporary Graduate visa base application charge is from AUD4,600.00.
A Subclass 485 applicant must be aged 35 years or under when applying, unless an exception applies.
A Subclass 485 applicant must have held a Student visa in the last 6 months.
A Subclass 485 applicant must have completed the relevant study in the 6 months immediately before applying.
The Post-Higher Education Work stream lets the visa holder bring family members.
The Second Post-Higher Education Work stream lets the visa holder bring family members.
entity: Subclass 485 Second Post-Higher Education Work stream

claim: DHA has a dedicated page for changes to the Temporary Graduate visa program from 1 July 2024.
The Temporary Activity visa is Subclass 408.
The Subclass 408 visa allows a person to come to Australia to do specific types of work on a short-term, temporary basis.
The Research Activities stream of Subclass 408 lets the holder and immediate family stay in Australia for up to 2 years.
The current DHA name of Subclass 482 is Skills in Demand visa.
caveats: Change history: this replaced the Temporary Skill Shortage naming in current DHA materials. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The Skills in Demand visa allows workers to stay in Australia for between 2 and 5 years.
The Skills in Demand visa requires the primary applicant to meet minimum English-language standards unless an exemption applies.
The Skills in Demand visa Labour Agreement stream says the holder can have their employer sponsor them for permanent residence through Subclass 186.
The skilled occupation list page includes the Skills in Demand visa Core Skills stream.
DHA’s median processing time for the Skilled temporary visa category was 63 days in April 2026.
caveats: Category median, not a Subclass-482-only band. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The Skilled Work Regional visa is Subclass 491.
The Subclass 491 visa lets the holder stay in Australia for 5 years.
The Subclass 491 visa base application charge is from AUD4,910.00.
The Subclass 491 visa requires state or territory nomination or eligible family-member sponsorship.
The Subclass 491 visa lets the holder live, work and study in a designated regional area of Australia.
The permanent regional follow-on visa is Subclass 191.
The Subclass 191 Regional Provisional stream base application charge is from AUD505.00.
caveats: This row is for the Regional Provisional stream, not the Hong Kong stream. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: A Subclass 191 applicant must have had taxable income at or above a specific income threshold for at least 3 years while holding an eligible visa.
The Skilled Independent points-tested visa is Subclass 189.
The Subclass 189 points-tested stream lets invited workers live and work permanently anywhere in Australia.
The Subclass 189 points-tested stream base application charge is from AUD4,910.00.
The Skilled Nominated visa is Subclass 190.
The Subclass 190 visa lets nominated skilled workers live and work in Australia as permanent residents.
The Employer Nomination Scheme visa is Subclass 186.
The Subclass 186 visa lets skilled workers nominated by an employer live in Australia permanently.
The Subclass 186 visa base application charge is from AUD4,910.00.
The current DHA name of Subclass 858 is National Innovation visa.
caveats: Change history: current DHA materials use National Innovation visa for Subclass 858 rather than older market labels. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The National Innovation visa is a permanent visa for exceptionally talented migrants from across the world.
An invitation is needed to apply for the National Innovation visa.
The Visitor visa Tourist stream for offshore applicants lets a person visit Australia for up to 12 months as a tourist, to go on a cruise, or to see family and friends.
DHA’s median processing time for the Visitor visa category was less than 1 day in April 2026.
caveats: This median combines subclasses 600, 601 and 651 and DHA says Subclass 600 can take significantly longer. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: The My Health Declarations service allows a client to complete health examinations before submitting a visa application.
If a client does not use My Health Declarations, they must wait until after lodging the visa application and being provided a HAP ID to complete health examinations.
If a visa application was lodged online, the HAP ID is in the referral letter downloaded when the application was made.
Health examination results are generally valid for 12 months.
After health examinations, the panel physician records the results and makes a recommendation to DHA about the applicant’s health status.
The panel physician will not tell the applicant whether they meet the health requirement.
If health results show no significant health conditions, the health case may be cleared without referral to a Medical Officer of the Commonwealth.
If a health case is referred to a Medical Officer of the Commonwealth, the officer may conclude that the applicant meets the requirement, will meet it with a health undertaking, or does not meet it.
DHA says the health requirement protects the Australian community from public-health risks, especially active tuberculosis.
DHA says a health undertaking may be requested for inactive tuberculosis.
DHA says a health undertaking may be requested for HIV.
DHA says a health undertaking may be requested for hepatitis B or hepatitis C.
The current Significant Cost Threshold is AUD86,000.
caveats: DHA says the threshold is reviewed biennially. Verified 2026-06-05.

claim: Temporary visa applicants aged 11 years or older can be required to undergo a chest x-ray.
Temporary visa applicants aged 15 years or older can be required to undergo serum creatinine/eGFR testing.
Temporary visa applicants are not normally required to undergo HIV testing except for certain groups or when clinically indicated.

All visa applicants who reach an age milestone after the immigration medical examination but before visa grant must undertake any further examinations required for the age milestone reached.
A parent or guardian must be present when a child is being examined or during blood collection.
A pregnancy health undertaking is required for pregnant visa applicants who have not had the required chest x-ray.

claim: ImmiAccount is the DHA online service used to apply, notify changes, check status or withdraw an application.
The Document Checklist Tool is intended to be used before lodging a Student visa application to find out what documents must be attached.
Answers to the Genuine Student questions must be written in English.
The maximum length for each Genuine Student response is 150 words.
There is an additional Genuine Student question for applicants who previously held a Student visa.
There is an additional Genuine Student question for applicants lodging in Australia from a non-student visa.
If the student or agent organised OSHC, the application form requires the name of the health insurer, the policy start and finish dates, and the policy number.
If the education provider arranged OSHC, the application form requires the insurer name and the policy start and finish dates, but not the policy number.
From 1 January 2025, onshore Student visa applicants must lodge with a Confirmation of Enrolment rather than a Letter of Offer.
A current surcharge of 1.40% applies to Visa card payments for visa application charges.
A current surcharge of 1.40% applies to MasterCard payments for visa application charges.
A current surcharge of 1.01% applies to PayPal payments for visa application charges.
If an applicant applied online, ImmiAccount shows health-assessment processing information through “View health assessment” in the “View application status” section.
DHA’s current processing page says offshore Student visa applications lodged on or after 14 November 2025 are processed according to Ministerial Direction 115.
